Security</div><div class="sc-e907e6ed-1 hsxxlJ"><p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-small" data-encore-id="type">Posted <!-- -->February 6, 2026</p></div><div class="sc-e907e6ed-1 hsxxlJ"><div class="sc-e907e6ed-2 jcTfNG"><img class="e-10202-legacy-image e-10202-legacy-image--circle e-10202-legacy-image--crop" style="--encore-image-inline-size:55px;--encore-image-block-size:55px" src="/images/avatars/spotify.png" data-encore-id="image"></div><div><p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type">Spotify</p></div></div><p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">Since day one, Spotify has been committed to safeguarding artists and their intellectual property. As the industry has evolved, so should Spotify's developer platform.</p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">Over time, advances in automation and AI have fundamentally altered the usage patterns and risk profile of developer access, and at Spotify's current scale these risks now require more structured controls.</p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">In response, we are making changes to <em>Spotify for Developers</em> to better protect creators, partners, listeners and the platform. These updates build on changes we've implemented in the past, including the <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="/blog/2021-05-27-improving-the-developer-and-user-experience-for-third-party-apps">introduction of developer modes</a>, <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="/blog/2024-11-27-changes-to-the-web-api">refining access for WebAPI endpoints</a>, <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="/blog/2025-04-15-updating-the-criteria-for-web-api-extended-access">introducing new extended quota mode criteria</a>, as well as <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="/blog/2025-02-12-increasing-the-security-requirements-for-integrating-with-spotify">deprecating outdated OAuth flows</a>.</p>
<div class="sc-7a365619-1 ergrQD"><h2 class="e-10202-text encore-text-title-medium" data-encore-id="text" id="whats-changing">What's changing</h2></div>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">Going forward, <strong>Development Mode</strong> <strong>will be reduced in scope</strong> while continuing to support learning, experimentation, and personal projects for non-commercial use by individual developers. These changes aim to preserve a space for tinkering and education while aligning access with these intended use cases.</p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">Starting <strong>Wednesday, 11 February</strong>, all newly created Development Mode Client IDs will be created under the updated Development Mode rules and will have the following restrictions applied by default:</p>
<ul class="e-10202-type-list" role="list" data-encore-id="typeList">
<li class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium e-10202-type-list-item" data-encore-id="typeListItem">Development Mode use will require a Spotify Premium account</li>
<li class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium e-10202-type-list-item" data-encore-id="typeListItem">Developers will be limited to one Development Mode Client ID</li>
<li class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium e-10202-type-list-item" data-encore-id="typeListItem">Each Client ID will be limited to up to five authorized users</li>
<li class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium e-10202-type-list-item" data-encore-id="typeListItem">API access will be limited to a smaller set of <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="/documentation/web-api/references/changes/february-2026">supported endpoints</a></li>
</ul>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">From <strong>March 9</strong>, these same requirements will also apply to <strong>all existing Development Mode integrations</strong>.</p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">For individual and hobbyist developers, this update means Spotify will continue to support experimentation and personal projects, but within more clearly defined limits. Development Mode provides a sandboxed environment for learning and experimentation. It is intentionally limited and should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business on Spotify.</p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">For detailed steps on how to adapt your integration to the changes outlined above, please refer to the <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="/documentation/web-api/tutorials/february-2026-migration-guide">migration guide</a>.</p>
<div class="sc-7a365619-1 ergrQD"><h2 class="e-10202-text encore-text-title-medium" data-encore-id="text" id="whats-next">What's next</h2></div>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">Protecting artists, creators, authors, listeners and the Spotify platform requires ongoing oversight of how developer access works. We'll continue to evolve this model and share updates as further changes are introduced over time.</p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">Continue the conversation on the <a class="e-10202-text-link e-10202-overflow-wrap-anywhere encore-internal-color-text-positive e-10202-text-link--use-focus" data-encore-id="textLink" href="https://community.spotify.com/t5/Community-Prep/February-2026-Spotify-for-Developers-update-thread/m-p/7330564">Spotify Developer Community forum</a>.</p>
<div class="sc-7a365619-1 ergrQD"><h2 class="e-10202-text encore-text-title-medium" data-encore-id="text" id="update">Update</h2></div>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px"><strong>March 9: Postponed endpoint access changes for existing integrations</strong></p>
<p class="e-10202-text encore-text-body-medium" data-encore-id="type" style="padding-block-end:12px">After some review and feedback from the community, we have decided to postpone endpoint access changes for existing integrations. The Spotify Premium requirement, the authorized user cap and one Client ID per developer limit will take effect as planned for existing Development Mode integrations. We will share further details on updated timelines as soon as we're able to share more.</p></div></div></main></div><footer class="sc-79176060-0 cDJEMg encore-inverted-dark-set"><h2
